newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's NAB posts another record profit.
newsitem.headline: Australia's NAB posts another record profit.

text.p: Australia's largest bank, National Australia Bank Ltd., reported Thursday its fourth consecutive record annual profit and chalked up yet another record profit for an Australian listed company in the process.

The Melbourne-based bank, which has operations around the world, reported a net profit of A$2.10 billion ($1.7 billion) for the year to Sept. 30. Managing Director Don Argus said he was confident performance would improve in spite of stiff competition in all markets and subdued economic activity.
NAB shares also hit a record high on the results.
"We are focused on the fundamentals of our business," Argus said in a statement. "We also have a vast potential market through our international spread of business units."
But he later told reporters that profit improvements would be hard won with interest margins remaining under pressure.
NAB also announced plans to buy back about 13 million of its ordinary shares, representing 0.9 percent of its issued capital, at an estimated cost of A$181 million ($146.6 million).
Analysts reacted positively to buyback news and the better-than-expected result, which some said was largely due to a lower effective tax rate.
"The actual core earnings were probably in line with expectations," said a Sydney analyst.
NAB shares finished 27 cents Australian (21.9 cents) higher at a record close of A$14.19 ($11.49) after touching A$14.22 ($11.52).
The bank said its Australian banking operations reported a slightly lower profit but operations in the United States, New Zealand and Britain made strong profit contributions.
Offshore units accounted for 86 percent of the A$133 million ($107.7 million) rise in group profits last year.
But Argus defended the Australian result as creditable amid difficult trading conditions.
"Competition in Australia was stronger than in any other market in which the group operated during the year," he said, noting domestic interest margins fell to 3.7 percent from 4.3 percent.
The bank's U.S. unit, Michigan National, bought for A$2.1 billion ($1.7 billion) late last year, posted an operating profit of A$158 million ($128.0 million), before amortization and goodwill.
Argus forecast better economies of scale at the bank's United Kingdom and Irish operations, adding the potential upside from the four banks in the region was "huge."

NAB owns the Clydedale and Yorkshire banks in the United Kingdom, National Irish Bank in Ireland and the Northern Bank in Northern Ireland. The bank said operating profit for its U.K. and Ireland operations slipped 4 percent to A$403 million ($326.4 million).
NAB's Asian activities, while representing a small proportion of offshore earnings, were seen expanding, he said.
